review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the upstream `gradedSimpleClassBasis_apply` and `gradedSimpleClassBasis_repr_apply` in SimpleBasis.lean, and the downstream uses in PathAlgebra/GradedSimple.lean. The file has two simp lemmas, `gradedIdempotentHeadBasis_apply` and `gradedIdempotentHeadBasis_repr_apply`. Both unfold a basis evaluation into a concrete class or coordinate. Their left-hand sides contain every hypothesis argument, so simp can unify them. Neither right-hand side contains the left-hand side's head symbol, so I see no rewrite cycle. `gradedIdempotentHeadBasis` is a plain `def`, so the upstream `gradedSimpleClassBasis_*` simp lemmas do not compete with these two unless the definition is unfolded. Downstream wrappers (`gradedVertexSimpleClassBasis_apply` and the zigzag analogues) forward to these lemmas and are themselves simp lemmas, which is consistent. The right-hand side of the `_apply` lemma writes out the structure literal rather than the private `headFamily`. That keeps the statement usable outside the file, so I count it as deliberate. I found no missing canonical simp lemma, wrong orientation or unwanted expansion. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out simp failures caused by instance mismatches.
